source.title: Minimizing Layerwise Activation Norm Improves Generalization in Federated Learning
source.authors: M. Yashwanth; Gaurav Kumar Nayak; Harsh Rangwani; A. Singh; R. V. Babu; Anirban Chakraborty

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. The text has apparent extraction/formatting errors in some equations, table headings, and figure captions.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests a different regularizer and uses global-model accuracy and Hessian eigenvalues to study generalization; it does not test the specific claim versions as stated.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy comparisons for adding MAN to federated optimizers, plus Hessian measurements. The optimizer/dataset accuracy results are extracted below. Values used only for hyperparameter selection and figure-only convergence curves are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study uses a flatness–generalization premise to develop MAN and reports its own method's performance. It tests none of V1–V8: in particular, raw Hessian eigenvalues and trace paired with accuracy do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gaps, or ranking against alternative measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the main conclusion: the authors claim MAN reduces Hessian curvature, improves federated-model accuracy and communication efficiency, and adds negligible computation. Their claim of consistent improvement needs a qualification: supplementary Table 5 reports CIFAR-10 FedDC accuracy decreasing from 83.64±0.13 to 83.59±0.15 at delta=0.3, a small difference within the reported variability.
record.recipe_differences: Federated learning with client-side activation-norm regularization; experiments use iid and non-iid client data, local epochs, and communication rounds. It does not use the original claim's random-label memorization or training–test-gap protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy results vary by dataset, client data partition, and federated optimizer. The paper reports a ζ sensitivity analysis for FedAvg+MAN on CIFAR-100 with non-iid δ = 0.3.

fits_no_version.finding: All 36 Table 1 comparisons report higher accuracy with MAN after 500 communication rounds on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding activation-norm regularization can improve reported accuracy of federated convolutional classifiers across several federated algorithms and client partitions.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 2 and 6 report lower raw Hessian top eigenvalues and traces with MAN. For CIFAR-100 at delta=0.3, FedAvg's top eigenvalue falls from 51.49 to 43.80 and trace from 8744 to 4397.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-norm regularization can reduce raw Hessian curvature in federated learning; these measurements do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The reported accuracy comparisons do not explicitly identify the accuracy as test accuracy or report training accuracy, so they do not establish a training–test gap. Figures 2, 3, 6, and 7 use a single training seed; Table 1 reports three initializations. The paper studies two principal datasets, with CIFAR-10 results in supplementary material.
record.rows_left_out: The reported 50%- or 28%-accuracy communication-round counts in Table 1 are omitted because the extracted measure is accuracy after 500 rounds. CIFAR-10 accuracy comparisons in supplementary Table 5 are omitted to keep within the 60-row cap; they report additional optimizer-by-partition results. Hessian top-eigenvalue and trace comparisons in Tables 2 and 6 are also omitted because the paper does not measure the magnitude-aware perturbation measure or training–test gap specified by the claim versions. Figure-only convergence curves are not separately transcribed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance under matched training recipes.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers, local connectivity, and transferred initialization.
Adaptive-gradient versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning and optimizer adaptations.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties; batch size is fixed at 50.
Dropout interventions, small-data regimes, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states concern V1–V8, not whether the numerical accuracy increases occur. Table 1 does not explicitly designate accuracy as test accuracy, although supplementary Figure 5 labels its sensitivity measure Test Accuracy. Section 5 says reported accuracy uses an average of all client models. No training–test gaps are reported. MAN strength is inconsistently documented: Section 4 gives dataset-specific values of 0.15 and 0.1, while supplementary Section 7 gives 0.6 by default for FedAvg+MAN. Omitted CIFAR-10, communication-cost, and Hessian results are already declared in rows_left_out and do not supply missing tests of these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width scaling beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under the specified tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to large-batch training.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
